correctness.rationale: Explicit x(t) solves superior logistic; z=1/y is a linear ODE and its integral identity gives exactly the critical quantity. Each y=h intersection is bottom-to-top because h' is strictly negative; thus there can be at most one interior peak. The sign of the exact reciprocal bracket and whether the weighted driving integral converges prove all r<=lambda and r>lambda cases, including equality. The derivative G'=C exp(F) delta'/a^2<0 proves uniqueness of the implicit peak. Leading integrals J~d zeta exp(-(r-lambda)t)/(r-lambda) and exp(F)delta/a~zeta d exp(-(r-lambda)t)/lambda prove both asymptotics. The standard-library checker reproduces an exact beta integral and independent peak values. Finite computations are supportive only.

value.rationale: In a competition-colonization disturbance recovery experiment, a large transient inferior population can be mistaken for a stable demographic response. The proved exact threshold separates overshoot from monotone recovery for identical ecological parameters, and its diverging logarithmic peak-time gives a strong monitoring-horizon effect. The critical exponent and boundary r=lambda link intrinsic recolonization and invasion relaxation time scales; the question is natural and the answer not a textbook equilibrium deduction.
